definitions.gloss: to crunch; to chew up; to bite into pieces
definitions.explanation: To break food or other objects into small pieces by biting. The literal meaning of chewing something hard until it breaks apart.

definitions.gloss: to explain in simple terms; to break down (an explanation)
definitions.explanation: To make a complex topic easy to understand by simplifying it. A figurative extension of the literal meaning.

examples.japanese: {氷|こおり}を{噛|か}み{砕|くだ}く。
{硬|かた}いせんべいを{噛|か}み{砕|くだ}いて{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I crunched up the hard rice cracker and ate it.

examples.japanese: {薬|くすり}を{噛|か}み{砕|くだ}かずに{水|みず}で{飲|の}み{込|こ}んでください。
examples.english: Please swallow the medicine with water without chewing it.

examples.japanese: {噛|か}み{砕|くだ}いて{説明|せつめい}する。
{先生|せんせい}は{難|むずか}しい{理論|りろん}を{噛|か}み{砕|くだ}いて{教|おし}えてくれた。
examples.english: The teacher broke down the difficult theory into simple terms for us.

examples.japanese: {専門用語|せんもんようご}を{使|つか}わず、{子供|こども}にも{分|わ}かるように{噛|か}み{砕|くだ}いた{説明|せつめい}を{心|こころ}がけている。
examples.english: I try to give explanations broken down simply enough for even children to understand, without using technical terms.

notes:
Godan verb (か row): {噛|か}み{砕|くだ}く・{噛|か}み{砕|くだ}きます
て-form: {噛|か}み{砕|くだ}いて
た-form: {噛|か}み{砕|くだ}いた

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {噛|か}み{砕|くだ}いて{説明|せつめい}する (to explain in plain language)
- {噛|か}み{砕|くだ}いた{表現|ひょうげん} (simplified expression)
- {噛|か}み{砕|くだ}いて{言|い}うと (to put it simply)

USAGE:
The figurative sense (sense 2) is very common and is a natural metaphor in Japanese. The te-form {噛|か}み{砕|くだ}いて is especially frequent as an adverbial modifier before verbs of explanation.
